headline.en: You're about to see your voice draw a wave. Keep it soft, in the middle of your voice.

detail.en: Tiny slurs, jaw and belly still
One easy long note, nothing steered

text.en: Follow the ribbon on a soft hum: a slow swing, then quicker and smaller.
Now one easy long hum. Nothing to steer: let it be.

measures.en: Your stars are for an easy, steady note. A real vibrato isn't steered: it grows from a note like this. Next: the easy note.

headline.en: A vibrato grows from steady breath and a free throat. It starts with an easy note.

detail.en: Like a relieved sigh, then hold it
Not quiet and breathy, never loud
Rest a fingertip on your chin. It should stay still

text.en: Sigh into "ah" and hold it, easy and steady, over the drone.

measures.en: Your stars are for a steady note held all the way. Did your chin stay still?

headline.en: A straight tone is how chords ring. It's light and calm, never a held throat.

detail.en: The same sigh, the same ease
No wave, like a calm horizon
If your throat tightens, let the wave back in

text.en: Hold a calm, straight "oo" for 4 seconds.
Now 6 seconds, still light.
And 8 seconds. Breathe whenever you need to.

measures.en: Your stars are for how long it stayed straight. If your throat tightens, let the wave back in.

headline.en: Before you shape your voice, train your ear: straight, a wave, a wobble.

text.en: Listen to each, as often as you like, then choose.

why.en: A stays on one line. B moves a little up and down: that's a wave.
Listen against the drone: a wave makes the note shimmer around it.
B's wave is small, but it's there. Smaller waves are harder to hear: you're training your ear.
B is slow and wide: a wobble. A natural vibrato is quicker and smaller, about five or six a second.

prompt.en: Which one is the natural vibrato?

why.en: B is quick, small and even. A is a wobble: slower and much wider.
It started straight, then the wave came in: a delayed vibrato. You'll sing it in unit 4.

measures.en: Your stars are for the rounds you heard right first time.

headline.en: Hymns and choirs often sing straight, so every chord rings clear.

detail.en: Straight comes from ease, not effort

text.en: After a bar of chords, sing the first line, every long note straight.

measures.en: Your stars are for the notes. Listen back: were the long ones calm and straight?

headline.en: A wave you steer is the gym for vibrato: slow and even first, then a little quicker. Tiny slurs between two notes. Jaw and belly still.

title.en: Rest a fingertip on your chin

text.en: Follow the ribbon: 2 a second, then 3, then 4.
Again, with an extra rung at 5 a second if you like. Stop whenever it feels tight.

measures.en: Your stars are for how even your waves were at 3 and 4 a second. The fastest rung is there to try.

headline.en: A natural vibrato is small. Keep the speed, and shrink the wave. Tiny slurs between two notes. Jaw and belly still.

text.en: At 4 a second: from a wide wave to a small one.

measures.en: Your stars are for staying inside the ribbon, evenly. Wider is never better.

headline.en: Hear a wave, then sing it back the same way: straight, or a wave at the same speed.

detail.en: Is it straight, or does it wave?

text.en: Warm up your ear: which is quicker?

why.en: B waves about four and a half times a second; A, three.
B swings further either side of the note. Wider isn't better: an easy, even width is the goal.

text.en: Echo 1: hear it with Hear it, then sing it the same.
Echo 2: a straight one.
Echo 3: quicker and smaller.

measures.en: Your stars are for matching the last echo's speed and size.

headline.en: Three held notes, a wave on each, and a steady straight step between them.

text.en: On do: a wave at 3 a second.
On mi.
On so: straight for a moment, then the wave.

measures.en: Your stars are for an even wave on so, after a straight start (unit 1's skill).

headline.en: Now the ribbon fades away. Keep the note going and let it settle on its own: a wave, or calm.

text.en: Follow the wave as it fades, then keep going on your own.

measures.en: Your stars are for a steady note after the ribbon fades, with a wave or without.

headline.en: Some vowels let the voice move more easily. Try three, at three easy heights. Tiny slurs, jaw still, never pushed.

text.en: "oo", a little below your note.
"oh", on your note.
"ah", a little above.

measures.en: Your stars are for steady, easy holds on all three. Listen back: which vowel moved most freely?

headline.en: Three long, easy notes. We'll describe what your voice does by itself: a natural vibrato, or a calm straight tone. Both are fine.

text.en: The first long note.
The second.
The third.

measures.en: Your stars are for three steady, easy holds. A vibrato is described when it comes, and it can take days.

headline.en: Shenandoah's last long "a-way": hold it easy, and let it happen.

text.en: After a bar of chords, sing "a-way", the long note easy.

measures.en: Your stars are for the long note: on pitch and steady. A wave is welcome, never needed.

headline.en: The delayed vibrato: start straight, then let the wave in. If no wave comes yet, a straight start still counts.

text.en: Hold "ah": straight for 2 seconds, then let the wave bloom.

measures.en: Your stars are for the straight start and the wave settling after it. No wave yet? The straight part still earns two stars.

headline.en: Choose on each note: straight, or with a wave. Listen to each one first with Hear it.

text.en: Note 1: straight.
Note 2: let the wave in after a moment.
Note 3: straight again.

measures.en: Your stars are for the last straight note: switching back is the skill.

headline.en: A choir sings straight so the chords ring; a folk singer lets the voice move. Same line, both ways.

text.en: The line, straight, like a choir.

measures.en: Your stars are for keeping the long notes straight.

text.en: Now free: the same line, and let "wide" move if it wants to.

measures.en: Your stars are for the notes and an easy long "wide". Listen back to the two.

headline.en: Everything at once: straight starts, and the long note blooming. Then hear how far you've come.

text.en: First, the long note alone: straight for 2 seconds, then let it bloom.
Now the whole line, the long "wide" blooming at the end.

measures.en: Your stars are for the line on pitch and the long note held. Listen back, then compare with your first wave in lesson 1.
